name: ATS-community fake-candidate sequence with shipping and endpoint changes

attribution.legal_posture: First-party employer, platform, or hiring-service disclosure with defensive guidance; legal attribution remains at source and service level.

caveats: Accent and other demographic or cultural proxies are intentionally excluded from the normalized control logic.

Ashby's community reports cover broad candidate fraud, including operations beyond DPRK cases. Accent, camera use, social-media absence, remote preference, and closed former employers are weak signals; nationality assessment requires source-backed evidence.
This record carries no identification or inference of an unnamed customer, applicant, identity-theft victim, or account.

Several controls overlap deep-first-party-platforms. The useful additions are ATS-community trend provenance and the sequence from application artifacts to changed shipping address and remote-management software.
Source-reported product or platform outcome statements require independent audit for efficacy claims.

statements: Ashby reports an increase in fake-candidate reports across its team and talent community and describes a sequence combining shallow professional accounts, copied resume content, identity and accent inconsistencies, remote-only constraints, later shipping-address changes, and remote-management software after hire.
Copy resume material from real professionals
Build accounts whose depth does not match the claimed career
Change the equipment shipping address after hire
limitations: Ashby's community reports cover broad candidate fraud, not only DPRK operations. Accent, camera use, social-media absence, remote preference, and closed former employers are weak signals and must never become nationality proxies.

Several controls overlap deep-first-party-platforms. The useful additions are ATS-community trend provenance and the sequence from application artifacts to changed shipping address and remote-management software.

statements: Complete background and employment verification before shipping equipment or granting access
Independently validate former employers and references
Use structured on-camera and live practical steps while allowing accessibility exceptions
Reconfirm identity and approved location at equipment shipment and first access
limitations: Signals require lawful, proportionate, accessible, privacy-preserving human review. Accent, ethnicity, nationality, visual similarity, camera behavior, geography, VPN use, remote work, or one device/network attribute must never act as a standalone detector.
